# Forms (FM)

This is the short form. Before writing code in this area, read the full rules with reasons, bad/good examples and checks: `.ui-polish/rules/07-forms.md`.

- **FM-01 Every input has a visible label** (warning). Each input, select and textarea has a visible `<label>` connected by `for`/`htmlFor` and `id` (or wrapping). The label sits above the field, is always visible, and names the data ("Work email"), not an instruction. Placeholders are optional examples of format (`name@company.com`), never the label. Where a visible label is impossible (a search box with a search icon button), use `aria-label`.
- **FM-02 Inputs declare type, autocomplete and input mode** (info). Set the right `type` (`email`, `tel`, `url`, `password`, `search`), `autocomplete` token (`email`, `name`, `given-name`, `street-address`, `postal-code`, `cc-number`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`) and `inputmode` (`numeric`, `decimal`) on every field, plus `name`. Disable `autocapitalize` and `spellcheck` on emails, usernames and codes.
- **FM-03 Validate at the right time** (warning). Do not show an error while the user is still typing a field for the first time. Validate a field when it loses focus (on blur); once a field is in the error state, re-validate on every change so the error clears the moment it is fixed. Validate everything again on submit, focus the first invalid field and scroll it into view. Constraints that can be shown ahead of time (password rules, character limit) appear as hints before any error.
- **FM-04 Error messages sit under the field and say how to fix it** (error). A field error is rendered directly below its input, in the destructive colour with an icon, linked with `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid="true"`; the input border changes too. The text states the problem and the fix in the user's terms ("Enter a date after 12 March", not "Invalid input"). A summary at the top is an addition for long forms, never a replacement. Server errors map back to their fields.
- **FM-05 Field width matches the expected answer** (warning). Size inputs to their content: postcode about 8 characters wide, CVC 4, year 6, phone 16, email and name 320 to 400px, free text full width of a constrained form column. Use a `<textarea>` (3 rows or more, vertically resizable) for multi-sentence answers. Forms are a single column, 400 to 640px wide; put two fields side by side only when they form one unit (first and last name, city and postcode).
- **FM-06 Mark optional fields; ask for less** (warning). Remove every field the product does not need now. When most fields are required, mark only the optional ones with "(optional)" after the label; when most are optional, mark the required ones with an asterisk plus a legend and `required` / `aria-required`. Never rely on the asterisk alone without a legend, and never mark both.
- **FM-07 Password and number fields behave** (warning). Passwords: a show/hide toggle button with `aria-label` and `aria-pressed`; requirements listed before typing and ticked off live; `autocomplete="new-password"` on sign-up, `current-password` on sign-in; paste allowed; no "confirm password" field when a show toggle exists. Numbers: use `type="text"` with `inputmode="numeric"` or `decimal` for codes, card numbers, quantities and money (avoid `type="number"` unless a stepper is wanted), accept pasted formatted values, show the unit or currency as an adornment, and right-align amounts.
- **FM-08 Submitting shows progress and cannot repeat** (error). The submit button is a real `<button type="submit">` inside a `<form>` (Enter submits). On submit it enters the loading state (ST-02), further clicks are ignored, and fields are not cleared. On success, confirm (ST-05) and move on; on failure, keep all input, show the error (FM-04) and re-enable the button. Do not disable the submit button to signal invalid input: leave it enabled and show what is missing when pressed. Label it with the action ("Create account"), never "Submit".
- **FM-09 Group, order and help** (info). Order fields the way people think about the task; group related fields under a short heading or `<fieldset>` with `<legend>`; split forms longer than about seven fields into titled sections or steps with progress. Put help text under the label as a hint, not in a tooltip. Destructive or secondary actions (Cancel, Delete) are visually quieter and separated from the primary button. Radio buttons for two to five exclusive options, a select or combobox above that, a switch only for settings that apply immediately.
